candidates.classification: New bounded 95e behavior and authority trace; related to the earlier open incident/UI/hostile contracts but no established historical alias or unique-count change.
candidates.trace: create_strategic_incident, after location and pending/dedupe checks, writes an incident-named CaseSiteAuthority, materializes an Active hostile group and roster, creates the pending StrategicIncident, and moves each living member and the party to that new site. The selected creator, hostile materializer, roster writer and occupancy setter do not create a matching CaseAuthority or an InvestigationLead. The incident site stores incident_id as its case_id. The exact source path is conditional on successful creation and on no separate producer already supplying the matching case/lead; collisions, other writers, transactions and every incident mode remain open.
candidates.first_failed_contract: If the incident site has no matching CaseAuthority, case_site_provenance_view and case_site_provenance_reducer both return None before classifying manual/generated cases. backend_case_site_pins requires an exact lead and that view provenance, so no pin can be emitted for that site under this condition. The selected web case-site enemy page requires that pin, and its tactical entry route also requires an active contract and matching pin. The native tactical-server request rejects missing provenance before binding; native autoresolve calls ensure_bound_mission_authority, whose fresh-mission path first requires exact_case_site_for_observer, which itself requires reducer provenance and an exact lead. Other earlier actor, scene, geography, readiness or mission-id guards may reject first. Therefore these selected current paths cannot enter that incident fight without an independently supplied valid authority, even though source-authored raiding/thievery descriptions describe a fight-or-flee choice. This is a source/control-flow conclusion, not a created incident, page observation or executed battle.
candidates.safeguards_and_limits: A source-only test specifies incident-owned lifecycle without quest side effects; it was read, not run. The repair must not fabricate a quest or overwrite the party active contract to satisfy a gate. Existing authority surrender can settle an arrest, while travel can avoid a pending interruption; selected simulation logic pays an affordable projected arrest then tracks origin for return. Those alternatives do not establish every intended player-facing incident outcome, ordinary web reachability, live state, or a complete post-fine hostile lifecycle.
candidates.connected_repair: After all remaining incident producers, public projections, web/direct callers, authorization, hostile roster, mission/resolution transitions, transaction semantics and intended rules are audited, give incident combat an explicit coherent authority and public handoff compatible with its non-quest lifecycle. Preserve source identity and the one-pending/dedupe gates, ordinary quest privacy, no quest side effects, tactical/transient boundary, avoidance and charge-scoped surrender; reconcile how party and hostile state finish together. Do not invent schema or implementation before audit completion.
